title: Rava of Parzakya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman considers him too to have taken a large part with Rav Ashi in arranging the Talmud, for he discusses matters with Rav Ashi, as in Yevamot 59b (where it reads “of Parkin,” erroneously, in Hyman’s judgment), Ketubot 39b, Nazir 38b (where it reads Ravina, erroneously, in Hyman’s judgment), Bava Kamma 36a, Bava Batra 4b and Zevachim 10b and 108.
We find in Eruvin 3a that he resolves Rabbah’s law, and Ravina resolved it differently.
He issued rulings, as in Pesachim 76b: a certain fish that was roasted with meat — Rava of Parzakya forbade eating it with kutach.
We find Huna Mar son of Rava of Parzakya, as in Ketubot 10a.

notes.text: The proposed emendations and claim of participating in arranging the Talmud remain Hyman’s. The supplied Zevachim 108 has no side; the invented a is removed. The fish-with-meat ruling and son Huna Mar remain separate statements.
The participation in arranging the Talmud and the proposed corrections of Parkin and Ravina are Hyman’s judgments; the supplied Zevachim 108 reference does not specify a side.
